message: To call the API, create an API key in the API Console and set it as an environment variable.
shared_wording: Create an API key on the API Keys page of the API Console. Set it as the PERPLEXITY_API_KEY environment variable.
question: Can every integration guide use this same setup step, or do some guides need their own wording, for example to set the key in a tool's own settings?
note: The docs name the place four ways: API Portal, API portal, API Console and Perplexity dashboard. The next step, setting the environment variable, is also written three ways, so it's in this row too. Changed from the research notes: their question asked whether API Portal is an older name for the API Console. The glossary has settled that since (API Portal and portal: avoid, use API Console), and audit check reports the name, so the question now asks about the step itself. One variant says "API Keys tab": check the screen before choosing page or tab.

message: The docs and the Help Center each explain how to sign in to the API Console, and the two pages should say the same thing.
shared_wording: Keep one page as the source and link to it from the other. Where both pages stay, share the steps word for word, for example: "Signing in creates a Perplexity account. It doesn't give you an API project or API access on its own."
question: Which of the two sign-in pages is the source of truth, and is the other meant to be retired?
note: The two pages are near-copies: the candidate list reports them as one copied_page row. Most rewordings swap API Portal for API Console, which the glossary now settles (API Portal: avoid, use API Console). Some change the meaning: the docs page says signing in doesn't create an API project, and the Help Center page says it doesn't give API access. The example joins both claims, so confirm both are true before using it. Heading case differs too (Signing In With SSO against Signing in with SSO).

message: An organization admin has turned this off for you, so you can't use it.
shared_wording: Use one set of statuses, always in this order, each with a one-line meaning. Connected. Connect. Upgrade required: your plan doesn't include this. Unavailable: this isn't available to your account, usually because of your role. Turned off by your organization: an organization admin has turned this off. Use Turned off by your organization for connectors, local file access and custom connectors alike.
question: Are "Disabled by your organization" and "Blocked by your organization" different admin controls, or the same policy shown with different words?
note: These labels come from the app, and they haven't been typed in from the app yet. Changing the help text alone would make it stop matching the screen, so the app labels need to change first or at the same time. Two pages list the statuses in different orders, and only the plugin troubleshooting page explains what each one means. Changed from the research notes: the status follows the glossary (Disabled: avoid, use turned off), and "an admin" became "an organization admin", the glossary term. The IDs here are the example strings; the labels appear on more pages than these.

message: You can't fix this yourself, so ask your organization admin and say what to ask for.
shared_wording: Ask your organization admin to [the specific action]. For example: Ask your organization admin to turn on desktop tools.
question: API project pages say "an Admin in your project": is that the same Admin role as in an Enterprise organization, or a separate role that needs its own name?
note: Help and docs name this person at least ten ways, including your administrator, your organization administrator, your organization admin and an administrator in your organization. The IDs here are four example strings, not every page. Changed from the research notes: "an admin in your organization" became "your organization admin", the glossary term (organization administrator, Enterprise admin and org admin are avoid). The notes' question asked whether Admin is a named role. The glossary now defines an organization admin as a member with the Admin role, so the question narrows to API projects.

message: Each plan has one line that says who it's for and what it gives you.
shared_wording: Use the same line on the pricing card, the pricing FAQ, the Help Center and the app. Free plan: Cited answers from the web, with [daily or weekly] limits. Perplexity Pro: Higher limits, top AI models and Computer, for serious work. Perplexity Max: The highest limits and newest models, for heavy, sustained work.
question: Is the Free plan's limit daily or weekly, and does it include basic AI models or the top ones?
note: The pricing card and the pricing FAQ on the same page disagree about the Free plan: daily against weekly limits, and basic against top AI models. The glossary's Free plan definition says weekly, taken from a Help Center article, so that half may already be settled. Confirm the facts in brackets before using the lines. Changed from the research notes: the plan labels use the glossary names (Free plan, Perplexity Pro, Perplexity Max) instead of Free, Pro and Max.

message: The Computer feature list says what Computer can do on Perplexity Pro and on Perplexity Max.
shared_wording: One feature list. A row both plans have reads the same on both, and a Perplexity Max row only says what's more. Both plans: Create and edit documents, slides and spreadsheets. Both plans: Connect 400+ apps. Perplexity Pro: Deep Research. Perplexity Max: Expert-level research and data analysis.
question: Do Perplexity Pro and Perplexity Max differ on documents and app connections, or only on limits and research depth?
note: The iOS rows are typed app strings from the Computer upgrade screen. They exist only in the app, so changing the pricing page alone won't fix them. The iOS screen lists expert-level research on the Pro tab, and the pricing page lists it for Max. Changed from the research notes: plan names follow the glossary (Perplexity Pro, Perplexity Max), and Deep Research keeps the glossary's capitals.

message: One line says what Teammates are, and one says who can use them.
shared_wording: Teammates are AI agents that own ongoing work. Optional second line: They keep working while you're away, using your tools and context. Availability: Research preview on Perplexity Max, Enterprise Pro and Enterprise Max.
question: Are "research preview" and "beta" the same status, and is the brand page's definition the one to follow?
note: The first line is already used word for word on two Help Center pages, and the brand page says nearly the same. The basis stays recommendation because the availability line is new. Two Help Center pages disagree on who can use Teammates: individual Max and Enterprise plans, against an Enterprise Pro or Max seat. The iOS lines are typed app strings and exist only in the app. Changed from the research notes: Max became Perplexity Max, the glossary name.

message: Connector pages say whether connected data is used to train AI models, and which security protections Enterprise organizations get.
shared_wording: A fixed block with one slot for the connector name. Heading: Will my [Connector] data be used to train AI models? Answer: No. [Connector] data, like all Enterprise data, is never used to train AI models. Then: Perplexity Enterprise organizations get SOC 2 Type II certification, end-to-end encryption, strict data privacy measures and granular user access controls.
question: Do these protections also apply to Perplexity Pro and Perplexity Max users of a connector, or only to Enterprise organizations?
note: Two of the four SOC 2 versions here leave out "For Enterprise organizations", which changes who the claim covers. The training question is asked four ways in these IDs. Changed from the research notes: three of the SOC 2 versions say enterprise-grade, which the glossary now marks avoid (name the control instead). The shared wording names the controls and doesn't use the word, and audit check reports it separately. "Enterprise organizations" became "Perplexity Enterprise organizations", the glossary term.

message: A connector or feature page says which plans include it.
shared_wording: Available on Perplexity Pro, Perplexity Max, Enterprise Pro and Enterprise Max. Always list the plans in that order, and leave out any plan that doesn't apply.
question: Is there a set order and a short form for plan names when they're listed together, such as Pro and Max without Perplexity?
note: The variants differ in the preposition (to, for, on), long or short plan names, and the final comma. Changed from the research notes: they suggested the short names Pro and Max. The glossary terms are Perplexity Pro and Perplexity Max, so the shared wording uses them until the team says a short form is fine in lists.

message: When a paid subscription ends, the account moves to the Free plan.
shared_wording: Your account moves to the Free plan when your current billing period ends.
question: When a payment fails, does the account move to the Free plan at the end of the grace window or at the end of the billing period?
note: Billing pages say free version and Free plan for the same thing. One variant is about cancelling, two are about a card that isn't added in time and one is about signing in with a different account, so the timing may differ. Changed from the research notes: their question asked whether Free is the plan's name. The glossary has since settled Free plan as the term to use, so the question now asks about timing.
